stem.en: A bus moves at 36 km/h. The driver sees an obstacle 30 m ahead, takes 0.5 s to react, and then brakes with an acceleration of -2.5 m/s². What happens?

feedback.en: Work out both parts: the distance in the reaction time and the braking distance. Their sum is less than 30 m.

text.en: The bus stops after 25 m, before the obstacle.

feedback.en: Right. 5 m while the driver reacts, then 20 m of braking: 25 m in all.

text.en: The bus stops exactly at 30 m.

feedback.en: Add the two parts again: 5 m + 20 m = 25 m, not 30 m.

explanation.en: 36 km/h = 10 m/s. In the 0.5 s reaction time, the bus moves 10 x 0.5 = 5 m. Braking: v² = u² + 2as gives 0 = 100 - 5s, so s = 20 m. Total: 25 m, so the bus stops 5 m before the obstacle.

hints.en: Change 36 km/h into m/s. Then add the reaction distance and the braking distance.
